title: Conveyor dead although the PLC says ON
summary: The PLC shows the motor command TRUE, yet the contactor does not pull in and the run lamp stays dark. Find out where the signal is lost.
objectives: Follow a signal from the program to the field device
Use module status LEDs and the diagnostic buffer
starterProgram:
PROGRAM Main
VAR_INPUT
    StartPB : BOOL; (* Start button S1, normally open: TRUE while pressed. *)
    StopPB : BOOL; (* Stop button S2, normally closed: TRUE while NOT pressed (wire-break safe). *)
    MotorFeedback : BOOL; (* Contactor auxiliary contact: TRUE when the contactor has pulled in. *)
    OverloadOK : BOOL; (* Overload relay contact, normally closed: TRUE while the motor is not overloaded. *)
END_VAR
VAR_OUTPUT
    MotorContactor : BOOL; (* Contactor coil K1: TRUE energizes the motor. *)
    RunLamp : BOOL; (* Green run lamp H1. *)
END_VAR
MotorContactor := (StartPB OR MotorContactor) AND StopPB AND OverloadOK;
RunLamp := MotorFeedback;
END_PROGRAM
instructions: Run the simulation and press Start; confirm the symptom.
Compare the PLC output tag, the output LED and the contactor.
Check the module status and the diagnostic buffer.
hints: The program is the one that worked yesterday.
An output module needs its own 24 V load supply to switch anything.

criteria.title: The motor runs after Start
criteria.onFail: The motor still does not run after Start.

criteria.title: The PLC commands the contactor
criteria.onFail: The contactor command did not follow Start.

troubleshooting.symptom: Pressing Start does nothing at the machine. On the programming device MotorContactor shows TRUE.

diagnosisOptions.label: The PLC program does not set the output
The digital output module has no load (field) supply

repairs.label: Replace the blown fuse in the output module's 24 V load supply

debrief.rootCause: The digital output module had lost its 24 V load (field) supply. The program and the CPU set the output correctly, but the module had no power to switch to its terminals, so the contactor coil never received voltage.
evidence: MotorContactor was TRUE in the PLC, so the program did its job and the fault lies after the output image.
The module status and the diagnostic buffer reported a missing field (load) supply for the output module.
Measuring the contactor's output channel gave 0 V while the output was commanded ON.
MotorFeedback stayed FALSE because the contactor never pulled in, which also kept the run lamp (driven by MotorFeedback) dark.
debrief.repair: Restore the output module's 24 V load supply (replace the blown fuse), then verify that Start runs the conveyor.
debrief.reasoning: Follow the signal in order: program value, output image, module, terminal, field device. When the PLC says ON but nothing switches, check the module's own supply and diagnostics before replacing field devices or changing the program.
